note: Centers at colleges and universities that study school choice or the new schools it pays for. Each activity is marked only where the center's own page or a primary source documents it. A blank means not documented, not proven absent. Funders are listed where the source names them.

centers.name: National Hybrid Schools Project
centers.unit: Coles College of Business, Education Economics Center
centers.what: Documents and analyzes hybrid schools and microschools, publishes original data, and convenes founders, researchers and policymakers at an annual national conference; the sixth is planned for Atlanta in April 2027.

centers.name: Homeschool Hub and Homeschool Research Lab
centers.unit: School of Education, Institute for Education Policy
centers.what: Publishes homeschool participation data for 39 states and state-by-state legal summaries; the lab curates research and convenes researchers. States that it is not an advocacy project.

centers.name: Center on Reinventing Public Education (CRPE)
centers.unit: Mary Lou Fulton College for Teaching and Learning Innovation, since 2022
centers.topic: School choice and new school models
centers.what: Joined ASU in February 2022. Tracked 372 district- and community-run learning pods through 2020–21 and studies school choice and new school models.

centers.name: REACH: National Center for Research on Education Access and Choice
centers.unit: Lead institution, with Michigan State and others
centers.what: Ran 48 studies, mostly on charter schools, and built the National Longitudinal School Database. The federal award closed in August 2025; data and publications remain public.

centers.name: Program on Education Policy and Governance (PEPG)
centers.what: Publishes research and helped establish Education Next; hosts national conferences including on school choice; has trained graduate and postdoctoral researchers since 2002.
centers.funders: EdChoice listed as affiliate and donor

centers.name: National Education Policy Center (NEPC)
centers.topic: Reviews of choice and reform research
centers.what: Publishes policy briefs and third-party reviews of think tank reports, many on school choice.
centers.funders: Funders include the NEA, AFT, Ford Foundation and Great Lakes Center

centers.name: Department of Education Reform
centers.unit: College of Education and Health Professions
centers.what: Sponsors school choice research and evaluations and funds ten doctoral fellowships.
centers.funders: $10M Windgate Charitable Foundation gift, matched by the Walton Family Foundation

centers.name: Center for Research on Education Outcomes (CREDO)
centers.unit: Founded 1999 at the University of Rochester
centers.what: Produces the national charter school outcome studies (16 states in 2009, 26 in 2013).

centers.name: Education Policy Innovation Collaborative (EPIC)
centers.topic: Michigan policy; was a REACH partner
centers.what: Was a partner in the federal REACH school choice center. Since 2025 its stated focus is the educator workforce: shortages, turnover, Grow Your Own programs and pay.
